page: Microsoft Azure F48amds_v7 is an x86_64 server instance powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processors operating at up to 4.5 GHz. The instance provisions 48 physical cores mapped to 48 vCPUs with a single thread per core, backed by 48 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates 384.0 GB of system memory, delivering an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Storage architecture features 5,669 GB of integrated local NVMe SSD capacity alongside support for Azure Premium Storage, with virtualization managed via Microsoft Hyper-V. Dedicated hardware accelerators are not present.

Benchmark assessments show top-tier computational and memory throughput across intensive workloads. In CPU benchmarks, the instance achieves top-decile scores in stress-ng single-core (3,765.29), stress-ng multi-core (175,742.28), PassMark CPU (98,150.08), and PassMark extended instructions (116,343.41), supported by hardware support for AVX-512 vector and neural network extensions. Memory subsystem performance demonstrates 9,285.95 GB/sec in cached small-block reads and 177.17 GB/sec in large-block uncached writes. The server also records top-tier results in Redis SET operations (130.02 million operations per second) and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (653.96 GB/sec), with static web serving throughput reaching 82.49 GB/sec.

The hardware configuration provides high resource density by combining 1:8 core-to-memory scaling with large local NVMe storage and dedicated execution cores. The lack of simultaneous multithreading avoids thread contention, ensuring consistent execution times for heavy compute tasks. A notable operational tradeoff is the reliance on CPU-only execution for machine learning tasks; while prompt and generation rates remain strong for small and medium language models, large parameter architectures (such as 70B models) demonstrate average CPU inference throughput.

Microsoft Azure F48amds_v7 is suitable for high-throughput in-memory caching layers, relational database engines requiring fast local scratch disks, enterprise data processing, heavy compression pipelines, and batch compilation workloads.

Synthetic and system benchmarks show top-tier multi-core computing power, marked by a PassMark CPU score of 98,150.08 and 130.02 million Redis SET operations per second.
